note: Hand-derived expected values; see README.md and tools/derive_fixtures.py. runs: [db, n] finite frames, [db, n, 'clipped'], [null, n] non-finite, ['gap', n] missing frames. 50 ms frames; 48 kHz timing (t_audio_ms = frame_index * 50). Not measurements of any real microphone.

cases.description: 100 ms transient (2 candidate frames) is rejected.
cases.derivation: Frames 10-11 are candidates (rel +10). 2 frames < 4: the segment is rejected when the 6th quiet frame ends it. No accepted segments.

cases.description: 150 ms transient (3 candidate frames) is rejected.
200 ms (4 frames) is accepted and the onset is backdated to the first candidate frame.
cases.derivation: Candidates are frames 10-13. Provisional onset = frame 10 = 500 ms (backdated: acceptance is only known at frame 13). End = end of frame 13 = 14*50 = 700 ms. Duration 200 ms.

cases.description: A gap of 5 non-candidate frames (250 ms) is bridged.
cases.derivation: Candidates 0-3, quiet 4-8 (5 frames, bridged: fewer than 6), candidates 9-10, then quiet. One segment, onset frame 0, last candidate frame 10, 6 candidate frames, end = 11*50 = 550 ms.

cases.description: A gap of 6 non-candidate frames (300 ms) ends the segment.
cases.derivation: Candidates 0-3; the 6th quiet frame (frame 9) ends the first segment at the end of frame 3 = 200 ms. Candidates 10-13 are a second segment [500, 700] ms.

cases.description: The segment ends at its last candidate frame, not after the hangover.
cases.derivation: Candidates are frames 2-5: onset 100 ms, end = 6*50 = 300 ms. The 30 quiet frames add no duration (not 300 + 250 or + 300).

cases.description: Three segments; longest run and sum.
cases.derivation: Seg A frames 0-3 [0,200]; 8 quiet frames (4-11) close it at the 6th. Seg B frames 12-21 [600,1100]; 7 quiet (22-28) close it at the 6th (frame 27). Seg C frames 29-34 [1450,1750]. Spans 200, 500, 300: longest 500, sum 1000.

cases.description: A segment still open when the stream ends is closed at its last candidate frame.
cases.derivation: 10 candidate frames, no offset seen. At finish the segment ends at the end of frame 9 = 500 ms and is marked unterminated (no offset observed).

cases.description: A frame exactly +6 dB above the floor is a candidate.
cases.derivation: -54 - (-60) = +6.00 >= 6: candidate. 4 frames accepted: onset 250 ms, end 450 ms.

cases.description: A frame at +5.99 dB is not a candidate, so there is no segment at all.
cases.derivation: -54.01 - (-60) = +5.99 < 6: never a candidate, so no segment is even opened (rejected count stays 0).

cases.description: A single non-finite frame inside speech is a bridged gap.
cases.derivation: Frames 0-1 candidates, frame 2 non-finite (non-candidate, gap of 1), frames 3-5 candidates. One segment frames 0-5 with 5 candidate frames, end = 6*50 = 300 ms.

cases.description: Six consecutive non-finite frames end the segment.
cases.derivation: 6 consecutive non-candidate (non-finite) frames end the first segment at 200 ms; the next 4 candidates are a second segment.

cases.description: A dropout of 2 missing frames inside speech is bridged.
cases.derivation: Candidates at indices 0-3; indices 4-5 missing (count as non-candidates, gap of 2); candidates at indices 6-7. One segment, 6 candidate frames, end = 8*50 = 400 ms.

cases.description: A dropout of 6 missing frames ends the segment.
cases.derivation: Indices 4-9 are missing: 6 non-candidates end the first segment at 200 ms. Candidates at 10-13 start a second segment.
